items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: While I was at Fort Custer I met Buddy Montgomery, who’s one of the fabulous Montgomery brothers, Wes, Buddy, and Monk.

ctx.x: Was in Michigan. I guess from your hometown they ship you to the nearest army base in your home state where you spend a transient period. Then you’re sent to where you go through basic training. While I was at Fort Custer I met Buddy Montgomery, who’s one of the fabulous Montgomery brothers, Wes, Buddy, and Monk. He was my bright spot during my early days in the army, being the brilliant pianist that he was. We had some nice jam sessions there at Fort Custer. Orders came for me to leave, to be shipped to Georgia,…

He said, “You play sick, because you don’t want to go to Georgia. That’s the heart of the South. You don’t want to go down there.” So I actually for the first time in my life played sick. I was so convincing. He helped me along. He said, “Can’t you see he’s sick? He can’t be shipped out.” So they changed my orders. The next time orders came through for me to be shipped out, they came through for California. I said, California sounds better than Georgia. So I was shipped to California for basic training to a place…
